case_title: Dakkata Balaram Reddy & Anr. v. State of Andhra Pradesh & Anr.
accused_socioeconomic_status: Not stated by the court; only a witness (PW-6) said A1 was a contractor who possessed 8 lorries
accused_victim_relationship: Acquaintance: the accused were customers of PW-1 (father/husband of the victims); no direct relationship with the victims is stated
statutory_provisions: IPC s.302, s.397, s.450 (convicted); charged also under ss.379, 394 r/w 397, 411
evidence_type: Circumstantial evidence, supported by eyewitness-type sightings of the accused running away, medical evidence, recovery of stolen property and arrest, identification of ornaments, and fingerprint evidence (rejected)
confession: A1 allegedly confessed to the police; only the part of the confession leading to recovery of the ornaments was relied on under s.27. A2 allegedly confessed, but the judgment does not rely on that confession
aggravating_circumstances: Killing of a mother and son with iron rods during a house robbery, as alleged by the prosecution and treated as homicidal
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under ss.302, 397 and 450 IPC; life imprisonment and fine of Rs 2,000 each under s.302; 10 years and Rs 2,000 fine each under s.450; 7 years under s.397; default imprisonment
high_court_outcome: Appeal dismissed; conviction and sentence confirmed
neutral_facts: On the night of 21 August 2008, two accused entered a house while the victim's father, who also ran a gold and silver business from the premises, was away. The accused concealed iron rods under their clothing and attacked two inmates, the victim's son and the victim's wife, who were both killed. Gold ornaments of about 3.5 kg and cash of Rs 18,340 were taken. The father returned to the house around 10 pm to 10:30 pm, after receiving word of loud cries from the house, and found the bodies in pools of blood near iron rods, with gold missing from the shop almirah and showcase. Neighbours had gathered outside. Three witnesses, independent of one another and with no known animosity toward the accused, each said they saw one or both accused running away from the house that night carrying bags. Medical officers recorded death from brain injury and haemorrhage following a head injury and found the deaths homicidal; blood-stained iron rods were found near the bodies. Following a written report lodged around 11 pm, police apprehended one accused at about 1.15 am carrying a bag containing gold ornaments and cash, and that accused allegedly confessed. The second accused was arrested at about 4 am and produced a bag with gold ornaments; blood-stained clothing was seized from both. The father identified the ornaments at an identification parade conducted with independent witnesses. Chance fingerprints lifted from the shop showcase and a plastic box were compared with the accused's specimen prints.
physical_harm: Death of the victim's son and wife from brain injury and haemorrhage following head injury (iron rod blows)
financial_property_loss: Gold ornaments of about 3.543 kg and cash of Rs 18,340
motive: alleged: robbery of gold ornaments and cash
key_evidence_accepted: Testimony of PWs 4, 6 and 10 that they saw the accused running away with bags; recovery of gold ornaments and cash from A2 and from A1's house; arrest timing; PW-1's identification of ornaments at TIP; medical evidence of homicidal death; blood-stained iron rods; A1's s.27 disclosure
witness_credibility: PWs 4, 6 and 10 found independent and without enmity; no explanation why three witnesses would falsely implicate the accused; minor discrepancies attributed to passage of time and discounted; PW-24's fingerprint evidence rejected as unreliable
post_offence_conduct: Running away with bags after the incident; A2 jumped from the upstairs of the house and fled holding a bag; both found later with stolen ornaments; A1 disclosed the location of the ornaments on arrest
custody_duration: Arrested 22.08.2008 (A2 at 01.15 am, A1 at about 04.00 am); duration in custody not stated
trial_duration: offence: 21.08.2008; trial judgment: 30.08.2016; High Court: 03.10.2018; Supreme Court: 21.04.2023
legal_representation: Accused: R. Basant, Sr. Adv., with G. N. Reddy, Manu Krishnan, V. Vishnoo C. Kashyap, Ravi Shankar (Advs.); State of Andhra Pradesh: Mahfooz Ahsan Nazki (counsel)
investigation_status: FIR/Crime No. 61 of 2008 registered; investigation completed; charge sheet filed; trial completed
procedural_irregularity: Fingerprint lifting and specimen taking not done per prescribed procedure (no report before credible witnesses); fingerprint evidence discarded
appeal_history: Trial court (30.08.2016): convicted and sentenced. High Court (03.10.2018): appeal dismissed, conviction upheld. Supreme Court: appeal dismissed
defence_argument: No street lighting evidence outside PW-1's house, so the witnesses could not have seen the accused running away with bags
legal_principle_applied: Circumstantial evidence test (chain must exclude innocence; 'must be' not 'may be' guilty); Art.136 interference only for manifest illegality or grave miscarriage of justice; concurrent findings not reappreciated; minor discrepancies after passage of time discounted
precedent_relied_upon: Pappu v. State of Uttar Pradesh (2022) 10 SCC 321; Sambhu Das alias Bijoy Das v. State of Assam (2010) 10 SCC 374; Hanumant Govind Nargundkar v. State of M.P. AIR 1952 SC 343; Karnel Singh v. State of M.P. (1995) 5 SCC 518
sentencing_rationale: Not applicable; the Supreme Court did not revisit sentence and found no patent illegality or manifest injustice warranting interference under Article 136
